setter.name: Derek
setter.evidence: 'as I said, I think it was Derek, the last chap I spoke to, as I said to him, for me the physique, it's the secondary thing' (00:14:00) and 'like I said to Derek, I get into this cycle of over-analyzing everything and changing the routine too often' (00:18:50).

prospect.name: Sam
prospect.occupation: Cyber security engineer in IT; desk-based
prospect.family_status: Lives with a long-term partner who formerly worked as a nurse and now works in care roles; expects to have children in the next couple of years
prospect.training_background: Sedentary through his teens, peaked at 117 kg, then dropped to 79-80 kg training for army selection, which he entered and left because of shin splints. Regained to 105-110 kg, then restarted roughly two and a half years ago and has trained four to six days a week without missing a week since. Mostly bodyweight and kettlebell work at home plus a 60 kg barbell; has cycled through push-pull-legs, upper-lower and full-body splits, changing routine whenever he loses interest. Currently 100 kg and targeting around 85 kg. Started kettlebells last November with an 8 kg bell. Two runs a week recently; caps out at an inefficient 2-3 km. Has never worked with a coach of any kind.
prospect.medical: Multiple joint issues, all volunteered: right shoulder acromioclavicular separation from a fall in 2018, re-injured in a second fall while ice skating a couple of years later, intermittently symptomatic for six to eight years; right elbow problems on and off; both shoulders and elbows aggravated by a period of 100-300 burpees every morning which he had to abandon in November. Left knee investigated by doctors around eighteen months ago and attributed to distal hamstring dysfunction with a recommendation to strengthen the hamstrings; he reports the knee has been symptom-free since switching to ballistic kettlebell swings. Left hip / sciatic area tender, which he attributes to his desk job. Shin splints ended his army basic training. No clinician clearance for the programme was sought or discussed.

signals: Defined by a former self he is trying to escape rather than a peak he is trying to exceed: 'one of the biggest things is I don't want to end up the way I used to be... I was so unfit and I just don't want to ever be like that again'

Carries visible regret about the earlier version of himself, to the point of discomfort: 'because I dislike the way I used to be so much... overweight people make me feel uncomfortable. It's how it represents the person that I used to be, and I don't like that'
Lost ground after a hard season — left army basic training with shin splints at his lightest weight and regained 25-30 kg

Counter-signals: he is currently training four to six days a week and has not missed a week in a long time, which is not typical rebuilder behaviour, and his stated goal is capability rather than restoration. Considered the_optimizer and rejected it because his stated driver is avoidance of a past self, not pursuit of a better one.

goals.text: Feel physically ready for any opportunity — 'someone asks me if they want to go for a hike or they want to try rock climbing... I just want to feel like every opportunity that comes my way, I feel ready to take it on'
Stop needing willpower to compensate for the body — 'it's my mental willpower that carries my body through things, whereas my body alone would not keep up'
Get to roughly 85 kg and reduce body fat while keeping muscle; explicitly the secondary goal
Be able to run 5-10 km with a friend who was recently drafted semi-professionally, instead of capping out at 2-3 km
Reach 30 in March at a point of maintaining rather than chasing — 'it's not chasing getting to a point, it's more maintaining that for the rest of my life'
Be a good example for children he expects to have in the next couple of years and be able to do things with them
Resolve the shoulder, elbow, hip and knee issues so joints stop capping his effort
Physical presence and cognitive sharpness at work as a career asset — 'if you are in the best shape in your company, or in business meetings, that does have power'
Explore properly on holiday rather than sitting on a beach, and eat well there without guilt
Stop managing his own programming — 'I'm a bit tired of managing my work and my job, my home, every aspect of my life, and I'm constantly analyzing my workouts'

pains.text: Over-analyses and changes his training routine too often, which he names himself as what holds him back
No external accountability, ever — 'for the last two years, it's always been on my own. Everything's always a solitary venture'
Long-standing right shoulder and elbow problems from an AC separation and two falls, aggravated by high-volume burpees, which cap how hard he can train
Poor cardiovascular capacity — cannot run more than an inefficient 2-3 km
Not progressing at the rate he expects despite training four to six days a week for two and a half years
Very little in savings and rebuilding after a difficult decade financially — 'my last kind of 10 years have been very complicated financially, and I'm kind of at the back end of fixing that now'

Eats his partner's leftovers to avoid waste and knows it undermines him — 'I end up eating the more to address the fact that we're not wasting anything... that is a problem that I know about that needs dealing with'
Hip and sciatic tenderness he attributes to a desk job
Discomfort around his former self that he extends to overweight people generally
Cannot enjoy food on holiday without guilt because he is still trying to lose fat

objections.raw_quote: No, I definitely wouldn't be able to pay it up front.
objections.rep_response: Ran the financial picture properly — asked what he could do, what he had available, whether he had a rainy-day fund, and what was left at the end of the month (about £1,200). Explained that splitting into six adds interest and recommended two or three instead. Never asked about credit cards or available credit.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I'll have to discuss it and have a think about it.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it cleanly — 'Outside of the thinking about that aspect, do you feel like, yeah, I do want to do this?' — got interest confirmed, asked what the partner would say, offered to bring her onto the call there and then, and then correctly reframed: 'would it be fair to say that it just comes down to finances rather than sort of getting approval?' The prospect agreed it was money.

objections.raw_quote: I do have my pay review in October. And depending on how much my salary increases, I could revisit it then, is probably the best thing I can say right now.
objections.rep_response: Tested the premise — 'So what if it doesn't? What if it goes the exact same way?' — then asked whether any route existed to start now, then argued that starting now would improve his showing at the salary review itself.

objections.raw_quote: I can't warrant that money. It's simple as that, really. It's not a, yeah, it's a non-starter at the moment.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without discounting or further pressure: 'Okay, sure. I appreciate you being honest about that. Like, of course, trying to help you make the best decision for yourself, but if you feel like, no, I shouldn't do this at the moment, then I would say we shouldn't.'

objections.raw_quote: No, no, it's definitely just a financial issue, that.
objections.rep_response: This was the rep testing for a hidden fear objection rather than the prospect raising one — 'Could it be that you have a little bit of an uncertainty around actually taking that step for yourself?' — asked immediately after the prospect had disclosed minimal savings and ten complicated financial years. The prospect rejected it flatly and the rep accepted the answer.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Described in principle only: 'when we would potentially split up into six, like six months, it would be a little bit more because then the interest is added. If we would split it up into two or three, then it wouldn't add this interest. That's, of course, what I would advise you to go for.' No instalment amount or plan total was stated. The prospect computed roughly £750/month himself from the £4,500 conversion.

evidence: Explicit and repeated no on affordability: 'If I'm like very realistic, it's not very likely that I'll be able to do that pricing', 'I can't warrant that money. It's simple as that, really. It's not a non-starter at the moment', and 'Well, then I would not be able to commit to it, would I?'
Asked directly whether any route existed to start now: 'No, not realistically now, I'm afraid.'
The rep closed it out rather than holding it open: 'if you feel like, no, I shouldn't do this at the moment, then I would say we shouldn't.'
No payment, no link, no follow-up call booked — only an open-ended invitation to reach out.

Counter-evidence toward a future close: intent was genuinely high throughout ('outside of kind of discussing the financial side, I would be interested'), the consequence frame landed hard ('I would be disappointed... I don't want to end up the way I used to be'), and a specific trigger exists in the October pay review.

Counter-evidence on the disposition call: the rep framed the parting as 'looking forward to getting you started somewhere in October', so this could be argued as follow_up. Recorded as lost because the prospect gave an unambiguous no, nothing was scheduled, and the reopening depends on an external event neither party controls.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a video for the prospect to try in the meantime; prospect to reach out after his October pay review if his salary increases enough. No call booked.

notable.note: The best-executed discovery in this batch — Phase 5 ran properly for the first time and produced the strongest emotional material in the corpus — lost to an affordability wall that a commitment check would have exposed forty minutes earlier. Two things a principal should see. First, the prospect disclosed an AC joint separation with six to eight years of recurrent right shoulder trouble, an elbow problem, a diagnosed hamstring dysfunction and sciatic tenderness, and was walked through a loaded ballistic kettlebell programme with no question about whether any clinician had cleared it. Second, this rep had offered a $200/month lower tier to a different prospect the previous day; here, facing a prospect who explicitly wanted to start and explicitly could not fund $6,000, he offered no tier at all and sent a free video instead. The rep also argued that buying now would improve the prospect's October salary review, to a man who had just disclosed minimal savings; the prospect named it — 'it's kind of the carrot and the stick situation, isn't it?'

quality.notes: Constant inversion of short turns, and several places where a rep question and the prospect's answer share one block. Clear examples: at 00:00:51 the rep's own opening question 'So tell me, what can we potentially help you out with, Sam?' sits under Sam's label; at 00:01:12 the rep's label carries Sam's account of his teenage years; at 00:24:25 a long passage attributed to Sam is his own but preceded by the rep's setup inside the same block; at 00:44:12 and 00:46:47 the two speakers alternate inside single blocks. Recurring transcription artefacts: 'Fathom' repeatedly substitutes for 'amount' or 'fat' (00:46:58, 00:47:06, 00:47:17), 'chin splints' for shin splints, and 'a line' for 'a lion' at 00:27:39. Roles read from content throughout.
